assumptions: One durable job, two execution generations, two retries, database clock0..6, application and database timezone offsets -2/0/2, and a two-tick delay/lease.
Committed job and lease writes are atomic. Original generation, owner and snapshot/payload fences remain required; decoded millisecond timestamps alone are not ABA authority.
Raw claim timestamps use the same column decoder as typed reads. Job timestamp-without-timezone comparison values are bound as UTC text; database-local SQL clock expressions own relative schedules.
Renewal waits may outlive their transaction-start lease. The new expiry is sampled after acquiring the job row; another generation cannot be overwritten.

No scheduler fairness, eventual execution, provider quiescence, unbounded clock behavior, DST transition semantics or TypeScript/SQL refinement is proved. Real PostgreSQL tests separately cover process and database timezone matrices and lock waits.
bounds.progress: No temporal or fairness claim. Each model permits stuttering and repeated failures.
